items.title: Original HAFERL x nonnative Collaborate on New Richard Cow Leather Shoes
items.summary:
A new collaboration shoe, the RICHARD COW LEATHER, is launching from Original HAFERL , a historic footwear manufacturer from the Allgäu region in Bavaria, southern Germany, and nonnative.

The base model, the RICHARD, is a mid-cut silhouette that carries on the legacy of the Haferlschuhe, a traditional shoe from the Allgäu region of southern Germany. Unlike the offset lacing typical of standard Haferl shoes, it features a distinctive center-laced design.

It uses the traditional Zwiegenäht (double stitch) construction, resulting in a durable and water-resistant finish. The upper materials are tailored to each colorway: the BLACK version is uniform in smooth leather, right down to the collar and lining. Meanwhile, the LT. BROWN utilizes suede leather, creating a striking contrast with the tan leather lining.

Furthermore, the meticulous attention to detail from both brands is evident in features like the lug-patterned Vibram® outsoles matched to the upper's tone, and the matte silver metal hooks at the collar. This pair seamlessly blends traditional European shoemaking with the nonnative philosophy.

The Original HAFERL x nonnative RICHARD COW LEATHER will be released on Saturday, November 28th at 11:00 AM at the nonnative shop, the nonnative shop Osaka, COVERCHORD Fukuoka, the COVERCHORD official online store , and select nonnative retailers. It will be available in two colors: LT. BROWN and BLACK. Priced at ¥86,900 (tax included), sizes range from 25 to 28.5 cm.

items.title: BIRKENSTOCK Celebrates the 40th Anniversary of Its Iconic London Style with the "Camden's Clubs" Collection
items.summary:
German footwear brand BIRKENSTOCK has unveiled "1774 Camden's Clubs," a new collection inspired by London's music, fashion, and subcultures. Building on four of the brand's signature models—the Arizona, London, Boston, and Maria—the collection features silver cone studs and glossy brushed leather. It adds a rebellious edge evocative of punk and grunge to classic silhouettes.

The collection takes its name from the legendary music clubs scattered throughout London's Camden neighborhood. It focuses on the city's creative soil, where music, fashion, and various subcultures have intersected from King's Road to Camden.

This is rooted in the London youth culture of the early 1990s. Around Camden Lock at the time, grunge, hippie, and romantic styles mixed. It was common to see outfits layering delicate materials like lace and chiffon paired with rugged boots or BIRKENSTOCK clogs. The unique contrast created by boldly combining different tastes was a signature style of London in that era.

In a 1993 article for *The New York Times*, fashion journalist Suzy Menkes also highlighted the hippie style revival at Camden Lock. She described outfits that paired lightweight fabrics like lace skirts and chiffon blouses with heavy stockings, Dr. Martens boots, and BIRKENSTOCK clogs. This collection can be seen as a modern reinterpretation of the fashion scene of that time, where these contrasting elements coexisted.

A standout in the collection is the London, which celebrates its 40th anniversary this year. Introduced in 1986 by Karl Birkenstock, it was the brand's first shoe to cover both…
items.t: BIRKENSTOCK Celebrates the 40th Anniversary of Its Iconic London Style with the "Camden's Clubs" Collection

items.title: Ki One Becomes the First Korean Distillery to Win IWSC's Worldwide Whiskey Producer Trophy
items.summary:
Summary 

Ki One Whisky Distillery won the IWSC 2026 Worldwide Whiskey Producer Trophy, an award given to a distillery's whole range rather than a single bottleTo make the shortlist, a producer has to enter at least three products, medal with every one and take at least two GoldsKi One went eight for eight on medals, with Ki One Eagle and Ki One Moon both winning Gold

Ki One Whisky Distillery has won the Worldwide Whiskey Producer Trophy at the IWSC 2026 Awards Ceremony, held November 24 at Outernet Live in London. The Namyangju-based distillery is the first from Korea to be shortlisted for the trophy and the first to win it. The award comes a year after Ki One Unicorn took the competition's top single-bottle honor, the Worldwide Whiskey Trophy.

The format of the Producer Trophy is what makes the win significant, because it judges a distillery's whole output rather than its single best bottle. Producers only reach the shortlist if they enter three or more products in the category, every one of those entries wins a medal, and at least two of the medals are Gold. The IWSC judging committee then reviews the finalists and picks a winner based on overall medal performance and the results of Trophy Judging.

Ki One cleared that bar comfortably this year. It entered eight whiskies and every one came away with a medal, including Golds for Ki One Eagle and Ki One Moon. The entries were judged double-blind by a panel drawn from more than 30 countries, as part of a competition that takes in around 5,000 wine and spirits entries from roughly 90 countries each year.

The shortlist…
items.t: Ki One Becomes the First Korean Distillery to Win IWSC's Worldwide Whiskey Producer Trophy

items.title: The Pearl White DJI Osmo Pocket 4P Turns High End Camera Tech Into an Everyday Style Essential
items.summary:
For decades, professional imaging equipment has adhered to a rigid, monochrome script: matte black, utilitarian, and distinctly industrial. Cameras were built to hide in the background of production sets rather than exist out in the open. But as creative tools have seamlessly integrated into daily life—flooding street style snaps, OOTD breakdowns, travel vlogs, and backstage EDC (everyday carry) dumps—a fundamental question has emerged: when your camera is as visible as your outfit, why must high-end gear still look like a traditional piece of tech clutter?

DJI answers that shift with the Osmo Pocket 4P Pearl White Edition, a device that treats design not as an afterthought, but as an intrinsic extension of modern personal style. Moving away from dark hardware, this release bridges high-performance filmmaking and lifestyle essentials.

Rather than looking like an isolated gadget pulled from a camera bag, the Pearl White finish incorporates a multi-layer mica pearlescent coating. As ambient light changes throughout the day, the surface subtly shifts with a soft-touch luminescence that feels elevated and intentional. It sits naturally in flat-lays next to silver jewelry, high-end leather goods, and designer eyewear, functioning just as smoothly as a style object as it does a capture device. By challenging the classic black industrial standard, DJI is redefining how imaging tools fit into fashion’s inner circle.

The Osmo Pocket 4P Pearl White shows that form and firepower can coexist effortlessly. Its refined, 230-gram body looks right at home in fashion week, concerts,…
items.t: The Pearl White DJI Osmo Pocket 4P Turns High End Camera Tech Into an Everyday Style Essential

Sony has officially released the first look at its upcoming World War II drama film 'The Nightingale'Real-life siblings Dakota and Elle Fanning share the screen for the first time to portray sisters resisting the Nazi occupation in FranceThe highly anticipated adaptation of Kristin Hannah's best-selling novel arrives in theaters on March 19

Sony has officially unveiled the trailer for The Nightingale , marking the very first time real-life sisters Dakota and Elle Fanning will share the screen together. Directed by Michael Morris, the highly anticipated cinematic adaptation of author Kristin Hannah's popular novel follows the siblings as they navigate survival and resistance in France during the World War II occupation by Nazi Germany.

Taking on the complex lead roles, Elle Fanning plays Isabelle Rossignol, while Dakota Fanning portrays Vianne Mauriac. According to the film's official logline, the gripping narrative delivers a "powerful, emotional story of two sisters forced to embark on separate courageous, dangerous paths in a fight for survival and freedom during World War II." While the sisters previously both appeared in the 2001 film I Am Sam, Elle played an infant version of Dakota's character, meaning the two never actually acted opposite one another on camera.

The star-studded historical ensemble cast also features Edmund Donovan, Shira Haas as Rachel de Champlain, Mark Rylance as Julien Rossignol, Albrecht Schuch, Douglas Hodge, Gwilym Lee, and Vinette Robinson. The screenplay was penned by Dana Stevens and Ann Peacock, with extensive production…
items.t: Real-Life Sisters Dakota and Elle Fanning Unite on Screen in Sony's World War II Drama 'The Nightingale'

items.title: Rare Hilma af Klint Masterpiece Commands a Record-Breaking $12.7 Million USD at Auction
items.summary:
Summary 

A 1920 abstract painting by pioneering artist Hilma af Klint recently sold for a record-breaking $12.7 million USD at a Swedish auction houseThe rare offering of 'Ser III No. 5' marks a historic moment for the artist whose foundation typically keeps her work strictly off the marketThe unprecedented sale sparked controversy among art historians who argue the esoteric work was never intended for commercial consumption

Pioneering artist Hilma af Klint has set a new posthumous record following the landmark sale of her 1920 abstraction, Ser III No. 5 . Hosted by the Bukowskis auction house in Stockholm, the extremely rare market appearance resulted in a staggering $12.7 million USD final price, a sum roughly 15 times its initial high estimate of $800,000 USD.

Held closely by a single unnamed family since 1995, the painting was originally acquired after the artist's foundation deaccessioned a small number of works. The sale adds a lucrative new chapter to af Klint's posthumous ascent. While the artist remained relatively obscure following her death in 1944, a series of blockbuster museum exhibitions in the 2010s—including a record-shattering 2018 showcase at the New York Guggenheim Museum—firmly repositioned her as a foundational inventor of European abstraction. Her enigmatic canvases, featuring dazzling arrays of curlicuing lines and inscrutable symbols, were famously created in response to spirits she contacted.

Because the foundation generally restricts her artwork from entering the commercial market, the recent Bukowskis auction sparked debate among art…

The official trailer for the highly anticipated period biopic, Maserati: The Brothers . Scheduled to hit the big screen early next year, the film chronicles the real-life story of how the titular family defied the odds to launch one of the most iconic luxury car manufacturers in Italian history.

The star-studded project features an acclaimed ensemble cast, including Al Pacino , Anthony Hopkins , Jessica Alba , and Andy Garcia . Taking on the pivotal roles of the visionary siblings, the movie stars Michele Morrone, Salvatore Esposito, and Lorenzo De Moor as the real-life Alfieri, Bindo, and Carlo Maserati, respectively.

According to the film's official synopsis, the movie carefully follows the Maserati family's journey starting from its initial founding in 1914. From those early days, the cinematic narrative tracks the brand's ambitious goal to revolutionize car racing, ultimately cementing its status as a renowned Italian luxury car manufacturer competing alongside historic rivals like Ferrari and Lamborghini.

Maserati: The Brothers officially releases in theaters on January 29, 2027.

items.title: VERDY and Mercedes-Benz Japan Unveil Final "VICK x G-Class" Collection
items.summary:
Summary 

VERDY and Mercedes-Benz Japan conclude their collaboration with a final capsule.Art car camo and VICK graphics debut on jackets, hoodies, cushions, and badges.It drops November 28 at Mercedes-Benz STUDIO TOKYO from approx. $11 USD to $208 USD.

Mercedes-Benz Japan has reunited with Japanese graphic artist VERDY to unveil the third and final capsule collection of their collaborative “VICK x G-Class” collection.

Building on their earlier drops, the closing release transforms VERDY’s original camouflage pattern, previously showcased on the collaboration’s custom art car, into merchandise for the first time. The pattern is also paired with his original character for the first time across a selection of accessories, highlighted by a cushion sized for in-car use. Rounding out the visual motifs is the signature “VICK x G-Class” graphic, which unites VERDY’s VICK character with the iconic G-Class . 

Key apparel offerings include the VERDY x Mercedes-Benz STUDIO TOKYO Jacket (¥33,000 JPY, approx. $208 USD) and the VICK x Mercedes-Benz STUDIO TOKYO ZIP hoodie (¥19,800 JPY, approx. $125 USD) featuring the “VICK x G-Class” artwork/ Completing the drop on the accessories front are the VERDY x Mercedes-Benz STUDIO TOKYO CUSHION (¥12,000 JPY, approx. $75 USD) and the VICK x G-Class Badge Set (¥1,800 JPY, approx. $11 USD).

The final VERDY x Mercedes-Benz Japan collection releases on November 28 exclusively at Mercedes-Benz STUDIO TOKYO.

items.title: Cherry Los Angeles' Holiday '26 Collection Is Made for the Long Way Home
items.summary:
Cherry Los Angeles is leaning into rugged Americana for its Holiday '26 collection, a winter range built around the kind of outdoor clothing that used to get handed down rather than replaced. The Los Angeles label focuses on hardwearing materials and careful construction, with pieces designed to look better the longer they're worn.

Outerwear leads the collection, starting with shearling aviators and leather jackets cut from a leather Cherry developed in-house to soften and take on character over time. Stone-washed canvas work jackets offer a lighter option with a broken-in look from day one. Under those heavier pieces, hand-loomed alpaca sweaters and garment-dyed heavyweight hoodies handle the mid-layer.

Thermals do much of the work in the rest of the range. The Best In The West, Ranchwear Boxy and Chevron Henley styles cover everything from western graphics to waffle-knit henleys, while the Frontier Henley Sherpa and Zip Up Sherpa Jacket add pile-lined warmth. Wide Leg Cargo Pants in Woodland Camo, a Plaid Western Shirt and an American Flag Knit Crew push the outdoorsman theme further. The women's lineup includes Knit Rugby shirts in Cabernet Red and Oatmeal, fitted T-shirts and eagle-graphic thermals.

The palette stays grounded in workwear tones such as Vintage Black, Smoke, Faded Navy, Oatmeal and Cabernet Red, with bursts of orange and camo. A full run of 5 Star and American Truckers plus 5- and 6-panel caps finishes off the look.

Cherry Los Angeles' Holiday '26 collection is available online and at Cherry stores.

Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
items.t: Cherry Los Angeles' Holiday '26 Collection Is Made for the Long Way Home

items.title: Children of the revolution: how the north of England is defining modern men’s fashion
items.summary:
Once the historic centre of the textile industry, the north is now home to a host of a provenance-driven labels. But is there a specific northern menswear look? And what does it all mean for the mad-fer-it stereotypes?

In 2026, clothing has proved more important to Andy Burnham’s political identity than that of any British prime minister since Margaret Thatcher. He is a loyal Clarks and Adidas wearer, whose Howick worker’s jacket hangs in Manchester’s People’s History Museum. His ousting of Keir Starmer – launched shortly before being photographed jogging in a replica Everton shirt – has been memorialised as the “casual coup”. In one telling, the reason for this is simple: he’s a man from the north.

That Burnham is the first born-and-bred northern male PM since Harold Wilson last swished his Gannex raincoat out of Downing Street goes some way to explaining his higher interest in clothing. It’s not necessarily that all men in the south care less about clothing, or that all men in the north do – but that many men from the north express it in such a distinctive, even unified, way.

items.title: Brioche armchairs, butter sculptures and edible chandeliers: meet the new food artists
items.summary:
Culinary artists are turning fashion shows and design fairs into a feast for the eyes

A pretty Venetian chandelier featuring delicate pink flowers and cascading blue leaves hangs from a ceiling. A hazy, warm light radiates from its tulip bulbs. Suddenly, a woman reaches up and snaps off one of the flower stems, giggling as she begins to nibble it. Welcome to the weird and wonderful world of Laila Gohar. The Egyptian-born, New York-based artist is part of a new wave of culinary artists blurring the lines between sustenance and spectacle, and this troupe have quickly become a firm fixture at fashion parties and design fairs, turning dining into a phenomenon and delight.

Gohar describes the chandelier, made entirely from hand-spun sugar (including the silver chain that suspended it) as her “favourite thing she has done in recent history”. It joins a long list of extravagant yet still edible installations she has created, including lifesize armchairs made of brioche, an entire room constructed with Belgian chocolate and a four-metre-long mortadella that had to be lifted into the party’s venue using a crane.

items.title: In a flap: how the butterfly became a symbol of gen Z resilience – and anxiety
items.summary:
The delicate insect has become fashion’s favourite motif again – but having represented sexuality in the 90s and the soul in Greco-Roman times, what does it say about youth culture today?

• Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

In the new Gucci campaign, Mariah Carey blows a goodbye kiss to 2026 in the most Mariahhhh way possible. Dressed in a fake fur coat and an azure dress, she enters a Christmas party to the twinkly sounds of All I Want For Christmas Is You. There are beautiful people, presents wrapped with Gucci string and butterflies, which have been associated with the popstar since her 1997 album, Butterfly, but have recently fluttered back to become a symbol of gen Z defiance and girlhood.

Carey serves as fairy godmother to the other “pop girlies” who have embraced the emblem, from PinkPantheress to Dua Lipa; Rachel Chinouriri to Marina and the Diamonds. At the Academy Museum gala in October, the singer Janelle Monáe looked as if she might take flight in a Robert Wun couture gown, with wide, yonic wings. Elsewhere, Tate McRae recently wore a black sequined butterfly bra and matching butterfly wing belt from lingerie wunderkind Ludovic de Saint Sernin. Both Swedish popstar Zara Larsson and her fans are championing glittery butterfly makeup motifs.
items.t: In a flap: how the butterfly became a symbol of gen Z resilience – and anxiety
